newsitem.title: USA: Early Fla citrus crops show first stage of color.
newsitem.headline: Early Fla citrus crops show first stage of color.

text.p: Many early crops have started to show the first stages of color break as groves, trees and new crop fruit continue in very good to excellent condition, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS) said.

Limited rainfall for the week ended September 29 prompted growers to run their irrigation equipment. Daytime temperatures were lower than in recent weeks with caretakers reporting highs in the upper 80s to low 90s (degrees Fahrenheit), FASS said.
Packing houses continue to test Navels, Ambersweet oranges, Fallglo tangerines, Satsumas, and both colored and white grapefruit.

Rainfall over the southern peninsula ranged from no rainfall to an inch in limited areas. Temperatures for the week averaged one-to-three degrees Fahrenheit below normal in some western and Panhandle and northern Peninsula cities, FASS said.
